findings.reason: a node implementing the Deliverable literally (widening the covering set, which is what the same function's comment "Every stored review that raises this finding is a covering review" already asserts) reds its own case 2 and must then make a design decision the plan does not settle — whether the ambiguity refusal is removed outright, or scoped so it never fires when a newest review can be chosen — which is precisely the blocker the brief says to report rather than guess at.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires that "an answer given without `--review-run` is written to the newest review raising that finding id and never to an older one", but `crew review --answer` refuses exactly that case today: once the covering set is widened to the "any delivered review … that raises the named finding" the same Deliverable demands, done-when case 2 (two reviews at one `plan_version`, both raising `wiring-1`, answered without `--review-run`) reaches `elif len(covering) > 1:` at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2792` and exits 1 with "finding 'wiring-1' is carried by 2 covering reviews; name --review-run to choose which one answers it", so case 2 cannot pass while that branch stands, and the plan never says the ambiguity refusal is replaced by "prefer the newest".
